Common baseline patience
All arrangements share the same baseline psychological discount rate. Differences concern modeled effective temporal weighting, not assigned differences in intrinsic patience.
A focal holder
The decision-maker is one holder allocating attention. Provider and manager choices are not solved separately, and outcomes are not population averages.
Instrumental choice
The holder minimizes the specified recurring costs net of benefits. Habit, errors, and psychological switching costs are not separate mechanisms.
Substantive engagement

Engagement jointly maintains competence and understanding. Relevant macroeconomic, monetary, institutional, custody, and protocol learning can qualify; community participation or conviction alone does not demonstrate learning.
Monitoring and engagement

Financial review is a distinct activity and implies neither trading nor pressure to act. Social platforms can support either activity. Dual-purpose activity requires attribution without counting the same time twice.
A limited resource budget
Engagement and monitoring share a fixed attention budget. Unused resources retain outside value. A larger position does not automatically expand the budget.
Substitution and bounded complementarity

The core has competing attention uses. A tested variant lowers joint effort costs when both engagement and monitoring occur. It can increase engagement in response to monitoring incentives when attention is slack; a binding budget still forces a tradeoff.
Smooth and strictly convex choice
Positive own activity costs and complementarity below the stated bound yield one global optimum, including activity and budget boundaries. Fixed entry costs and multiple equilibria are absent.
Independent practical benefits
Engagement reduces separately specified operational and interpretation mistakes and supports readiness to exercise available rights. Selling early is not intrinsically an error.
Conditional stake benefits

Proportional payoff growth remains one benchmark. Zero-growth and subproportional alternatives share a common comparison point. Position value, Bitcoin quantity, and wealth share are distinct; the model does not separately identify them.
Binary transfer authority
Independent authority either permits transfer without the relevant intermediary's authorization or is absent. The variable is not a self-custody portfolio fraction.
Control creates an engagement payoff
Independent authority increases the practical return to competence. It does not enter the discount-rate equation directly.
Operational assistance and pressure buffering

Support reduces a specified operational burden. Its separate pressure-buffer productivity is varied from zero upward. Fees, provider misconduct, and new counterparty failure risks remain outside the support function; assistance does not establish temporal benefits.
No delegated commitment substitute
Support cannot replenish the holder's commitment stock or reproduce independent transfer. Optional education increases the productivity of actual engagement and is zero in the reference cases.
Financial review has instrumental rewards
Monitoring offers diminishing benefits. Its payoff may grow with position value under a specified elasticity. This is not a preference for immediate consumption and is not estimated from data.
Pressure requires an explicit connection

Monitoring creates additional decision-relevant pressure only through the arrangement loading lambda. Routine review can have zero loading. External obligations are possible but zero in the reference cases.
A conditional capacity buffer

Holder engagement contributes to the capacity buffer. Provider support contributes only when its assumed buffering productivity is positive. The zero-buffer case retains operational assistance. Capacity does not measure control rights or reproduce independent exit.
Maintained understanding depreciates
Actual engagement replenishes a stock that otherwise erodes. Pressure can accelerate erosion. Existing understanding decays gradually; it does not vanish on a custodial transfer.
Commitment weighting is a hypothesis

Greater maintained commitment lowers the effective rate only when its assumed strength kappa is positive. Strengths of zero, 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 are compared. The old 25% asymptote is an illustrative boundary, not a finding.
Pressure weighting is a hypothesis
Pressure raises the effective rate through a specified pressure/capacity function when beta is positive. The reference uses a squared ratio. Operational capacity can reduce the effect.
Two interacting temporal paths

Commitment and pressure multipliers combine multiplicatively. Pressure also erodes commitment. Removing direct pressure weighting alone leaves that indirect path; both removals are reported separately.
No feedback from rates to effort
Effective rates do not enter the attention objective. The model does not solve lifetime consumption or an intertemporal optimal-control problem.
Stationary comparisons
Main outputs compare maintained steady states. Finite stock-adjustment lags do not establish permanent hysteresis or irreversible institutional lock-in.
Arrangements remain given
Portfolio splitting, wealth-dependent switching, entry into financialization, and changing worldviews remain outside the core. They are interpretation limits rather than new decision layers.
Ideal types and observable behavior differ

Orientation means priorities and admissibility criteria. Holding duration, no trading, visible wallet size, and a custodial transfer do not identify it. Mixed arrangements can coexist within one person's portfolio.
Comparable primitives
Reference cases share the attention budget and common technology. Differences in demographics, total wealth, risk preferences, prior knowledge, or selection are not estimated.
Illustrative numbers
Coefficients are uncalibrated and rates are normalized multiples of a common baseline. Scenario counts do not represent frequencies or probabilities in the Bitcoin population.
Bounded scope

Prices, returns, leverage, liquidation, consumption, aggregate concentration, provider strategy, and welfare are not endogenous. The model identifies conditional institutional mechanisms and cannot establish a universal empirical effect.
